questions.model_answer: When I have a tight deadline, the first thing I do is list every task and put them in order of importance. Then I block out time in my calendar so nobody can book meetings during that time. I try to stay on track by checking my progress every afternoon. If I think I will fall behind, I tell my manager early so we can find a solution together. Last month this approach helped me finish a report two days before the deadline.
questions.model_answer_ko: 빠듯한 마감일이 있으면 가장 먼저 모든 업무를 적고 중요도 순으로 정리해요. 그다음 캘린더에 시간을 막아 두어서 그 시간에는 회의가 잡히지 않게 해요. 매일 오후에 진행 상황을 확인하면서 일정을 지키려고 해요. 뒤처질 것 같으면 매니저에게 일찍 말해서 같이 해결책을 찾아요. 지난달에 이 방법 덕분에 보고서를 마감 이틀 전에 끝냈어요.

follow_ups.question: Have you ever missed a deadline?
follow_ups.sample_answer: Yes, once, because I underestimated how long the data check would take. I apologized and sent the report the next morning. Since then I add extra time to every estimate.

follow_ups.question: What helps you stay focused when you are under pressure?
follow_ups.question_ko: 압박 속에서 집중하는 데 무엇이 도움이 되나요?
follow_ups.sample_answer: I turn off my notifications and work in short blocks of 45 minutes. A short walk between blocks also helps me think clearly.

follow_ups.question: How do you ask for help when you are busy?
follow_ups.sample_answer: I explain exactly which part I need help with and when I need it. People usually say yes if the request is clear and small.

questions.question: What makes a good team member, in your opinion?

useful_phrases.text: In my opinion, the most important thing is...

questions.model_answer: In my opinion, the most important thing is being reliable. If someone says they will do something, they should really do it on time. A good team member also communicates clearly, so nobody is surprised by problems at the last minute. I also think it is important to listen to other people's ideas, even when you disagree. I have worked with a few people like that, and it made everyone's job easier.
questions.model_answer_ko: 제 생각엔 가장 중요한 건 믿을 수 있다는 거예요. 무언가를 하겠다고 말하면 제때 정말로 해야 해요. 좋은 팀원은 소통도 분명하게 해서 마지막 순간에 문제로 놀라는 사람이 없게 해요. 의견이 달라도 다른 사람의 아이디어를 들어 주는 것도 중요하다고 생각해요. 그런 사람들과 일한 적이 몇 번 있는데 모두의 일이 쉬워졌어요.

follow_ups.question: Do you prefer working alone or in a team?
follow_ups.question_ko: 혼자 일하는 것과 팀으로 일하는 것 중 어느 쪽이 좋아요?
follow_ups.sample_answer: I like a mix of both. I focus better alone, but I get better ideas when I talk with my team.

follow_ups.question: How do you deal with a teammate who does not do their part?
follow_ups.question_ko: 맡은 일을 안 하는 팀원은 어떻게 대하나요?
follow_ups.sample_answer: I talk to them privately first and ask if something is blocking them. If nothing changes, I would raise it with our manager.

follow_ups.question: Can you describe a successful team project?
follow_ups.sample_answer: We launched a new customer survey last year. Everyone had a clear role, and we finished a week early.

questions.question: Do you think working from home is better than working in an office?
questions.model_answer: I think there are pros and cons. When I work from home, I get more done because there are fewer interruptions, and I save about an hour of commuting. On the other hand, I sometimes feel lonely, and it is harder to build relationships with colleagues. That is why I prefer a hybrid schedule. I would like to work from home three days a week and go to the office on the other two days.
questions.model_answer_ko: 장단점이 있다고 생각해요. 집에서 일하면 방해가 적어서 일이 더 잘되고, 출퇴근 시간도 한 시간쯤 아낄 수 있어요. 반면에 가끔 외롭고 동료와 관계를 쌓기도 더 어려워요. 그래서 저는 하이브리드 근무를 선호해요. 일주일에 사흘은 집에서, 이틀은 사무실에서 일하고 싶어요.

follow_ups.question: What is your home workspace like?
follow_ups.sample_answer: I have a small desk in the corner of my living room. It is not perfect, but it is quiet in the morning.

follow_ups.question: How do you stay in touch with your team when you work remotely?
follow_ups.question_ko: 원격으로 일할 때 팀과 어떻게 연락을 유지하나요?
follow_ups.sample_answer: We have a short video call every morning and use a chat app during the day. I also try to have coffee with colleagues when we are in the office.

follow_ups.question: Do you think managers trust remote workers enough?
follow_ups.question_ko: 관리자들이 원격 근무자를 충분히 신뢰한다고 생각하나요?
follow_ups.sample_answer: Some do, but some still want to see people at their desks. I think results matter more than hours.

questions.question: How do you prepare before giving a presentation?

useful_phrases.text: I always start by thinking about my audience.
I practise out loud at least twice.
useful_phrases.ko: 적어도 두 번은 소리 내어 연습해요.

useful_phrases.text: It helps me feel more confident.

questions.model_answer: I always start by thinking about my audience and what they want to know. Then I make simple slides with only a few words on each one. I practise out loud at least twice, and sometimes I record myself to check my speed. On the day, I arrive early to test the equipment. All of this helps me feel more confident, although I still get a little nervous.
questions.model_answer_ko: 항상 청중과 그들이 알고 싶어 하는 것을 먼저 생각해요. 그다음 한 장에 단어 몇 개만 들어간 간단한 슬라이드를 만들어요. 적어도 두 번은 소리 내어 연습하고, 가끔은 녹음해서 말 속도를 확인해요. 당일에는 일찍 가서 장비를 테스트해요. 이 모든 게 자신감을 주지만 그래도 조금은 긴장해요.

follow_ups.question: Do you get nervous when you speak in front of people?
follow_ups.sample_answer: Yes, especially in the first minute. I take a deep breath and smile, and then it gets easier.

follow_ups.question: What was the best presentation you have ever seen?
follow_ups.sample_answer: A colleague told a short story about a customer before showing any numbers. It made the data much easier to remember.

follow_ups.question: How do you handle difficult questions from the audience?
follow_ups.sample_answer: I stay calm and say, That is a good question. If I do not know the answer, I promise to follow up after the meeting.

questions.question: Where do you see yourself in five years?

useful_phrases.text: In five years, I hope to be...
I would like to take on more responsibility.
To get there, I need to...

questions.model_answer: In five years, I hope to be a team leader in my current field. I would like to take on more responsibility and help junior colleagues grow. To get there, I need to improve my communication skills and my English. That is why I am studying every day. If I keep working hard, I think this goal is realistic.
questions.model_answer_ko: 5년 후엔 지금 분야에서 팀 리더가 되어 있으면 좋겠어요. 더 많은 책임을 맡고 후배들이 성장하도록 돕고 싶어요. 거기에 가려면 소통 능력과 영어를 늘려야 해요. 그래서 매일 공부하고 있어요. 계속 열심히 하면 이 목표는 현실적이라고 생각해요.

follow_ups.question: What skills do you want to develop?
follow_ups.sample_answer: I want to get better at managing people and at giving clear feedback. I also want to learn more about data analysis.

follow_ups.question: Has your career goal changed over the years?
follow_ups.sample_answer: Yes, a lot. When I was younger, I only cared about salary. Now I care more about learning and a good team.

follow_ups.question: Who has influenced your career the most?
follow_ups.question_ko: 커리어에 가장 큰 영향을 준 사람은 누구인가요?
follow_ups.sample_answer: My first manager. She was patient and taught me how to ask good questions.

questions.question: Tell me about a time you dealt with a difficult customer.
questions.question_ko: 까다로운 고객을 상대했던 경험을 말해 주세요.

useful_phrases.text: In the end, we managed to...

questions.model_answer: Last year a customer called because his order arrived two weeks late. He was very upset, so I listened carefully without interrupting. Then I apologized and checked the system to find out what had happened. I offered him a discount and promised a call the next day with an update. In the end, he stayed with our company, and he even thanked me.
questions.model_answer_ko: 작년에 한 고객이 주문이 2주 늦게 도착했다고 전화했어요. 매우 화가 나 있어서 끼어들지 않고 주의 깊게 들었어요. 그다음 사과하고 시스템에서 무슨 일이 있었는지 확인했어요. 할인을 제안하고 다음 날 진행 상황을 전화로 알려 주겠다고 약속했어요. 결국 그 고객은 우리 회사에 남았고 오히려 고맙다고까지 했어요.

follow_ups.question: How do you stay calm when someone is angry with you?
follow_ups.question_ko: 누가 화를 낼 때 어떻게 침착함을 유지하나요?
follow_ups.sample_answer: I remind myself that they are angry about the problem, not about me. I speak slowly and keep my voice low.

follow_ups.question: What would you say to a customer who wants a refund?
follow_ups.sample_answer: I would say, I am sorry about that. Let me check what I can do for you right now.

follow_ups.question: Do you think the customer is always right?
follow_ups.sample_answer: Not always, but they should always be treated with respect. A polite explanation usually solves the problem.

questions.question: Are you good at negotiating? Give an example.
questions.question_ko: 협상을 잘하는 편인가요? 예를 들어 주세요.

useful_phrases.text: I try to find a win-win solution.
useful_phrases.ko: 서로에게 이득이 되는 해결책을 찾으려 해요.

questions.model_answer: I think I am average, but I am getting better. I always try to find a win-win solution instead of just pushing for what I want. For example, last spring I asked my landlord to lower the rent increase. I said, Would it be possible to keep the same price if I sign for two years? He thought about it, and we met in the middle. I was happy because I saved some money and he kept a reliable tenant.
questions.model_answer_ko: 평균 정도지만 점점 나아지고 있다고 생각해요. 제가 원하는 것만 밀어붙이기보다 서로에게 이득이 되는 해결책을 찾으려고 해요. 예를 들어 작년 봄에 집주인에게 월세 인상을 낮춰 달라고 했어요. 2년 계약하면 같은 가격을 유지할 수 있을까요라고 물었어요. 그는 생각해 보더니 서로 중간에서 타협했어요. 저는 돈을 아꼈고 그는 믿을 만한 세입자를 지켜서 만족했어요.

follow_ups.question: What do you do when the other side says no?
follow_ups.sample_answer: I ask what their concern is. Often I can offer something small that solves it.

follow_ups.question: Is it easy for you to ask for a discount?
follow_ups.sample_answer: Not really. I feel a bit shy, but I have learned that the worst answer is just no.

follow_ups.question: What is the most important thing in a negotiation?
follow_ups.sample_answer: Preparation. If you know your limits and the other side's needs, you feel much more relaxed.

questions.question: How do you feel about meetings at your workplace?

useful_phrases.text: Many meetings could be an email.
A good meeting has a clear agenda.
We should end with clear action items.

questions.model_answer: Honestly, I think many meetings could be an email. A good meeting has a clear agenda and a time limit. People should come prepared, and we should end with clear action items, so everyone knows what to do next. I do enjoy short weekly meetings because they help me catch up with the team. But I get frustrated when a meeting goes on for two hours without a decision.
questions.model_answer_ko: 솔직히 많은 회의는 이메일로 충분하다고 생각해요. 좋은 회의에는 명확한 안건과 시간 제한이 있어요. 사람들이 준비해 오고 각자 다음에 할 일이 분명한 상태로 끝나야 해요. 짧은 주간 회의는 팀 소식을 따라잡는 데 도움이 돼서 좋아해요. 하지만 결정 없이 두 시간 동안 이어지는 회의는 답답해요.

follow_ups.question: Do you speak up a lot in meetings?
follow_ups.sample_answer: I speak when I have something useful to add. I am working on sharing my ideas earlier instead of waiting.

follow_ups.question: How would you improve your team's meetings?
follow_ups.sample_answer: I would send the agenda the day before and keep every meeting under 30 minutes.

follow_ups.question: What do you do when a colleague talks too long?
follow_ups.question_ko: 동료가 너무 길게 말하면 어떻게 하나요?
follow_ups.sample_answer: I politely say, That is a good point. Can we take it offline so we can move on?

questions.question: Tell me about the best trip you have ever taken.
questions.question_ko: 지금까지 가본 최고의 여행에 대해 말해 주세요.

useful_phrases.text: The best trip I have ever taken was to...

questions.model_answer: The best trip I have ever taken was to Jeju Island with my two best friends. We rented a car and drove around the coast for four days. What I loved most was the fresh seafood and the quiet beaches in the north. Unfortunately, it rained on the second day, so we visited a small museum instead. I would definitely go back, maybe in spring when the flowers are out.
questions.model_answer_ko: 제가 가본 최고의 여행은 가장 친한 친구 두 명과 함께한 제주도 여행이었어요. 차를 빌려서 나흘 동안 해안을 따라 돌았어요. 가장 좋았던 건 신선한 해산물과 북쪽의 조용한 해변이었어요. 아쉽게도 둘째 날 비가 와서 대신 작은 박물관에 갔어요. 꽃이 피는 봄에 꼭 다시 가고 싶어요.

follow_ups.question: Do you prefer planning every detail or being spontaneous?
follow_ups.question_ko: 모든 걸 계획하는 편인가요, 즉흥적인 편인가요?
follow_ups.sample_answer: I plan the hotels and the main sights, but I leave some free time. The best moments are often unplanned.

follow_ups.question: Has anything gone wrong on a trip?
follow_ups.question_ko: 여행 중 문제가 생긴 적 있나요?
follow_ups.sample_answer: Once I missed a train in Italy. I had to wait three hours, but I found a lovely cafe, so it was fine.

follow_ups.question: Where would you like to travel next?
follow_ups.sample_answer: I would love to visit Portugal. I have heard the food is great and the cities are very walkable.

questions.question: What do you do to stay healthy?

useful_phrases.text: It is hard to keep up, but...

questions.model_answer: I have been trying to build better habits over the past year. I make sure I walk for at least thirty minutes every day, usually after dinner. I also try to eat less fast food and drink more water. It is hard to keep up when I am busy at work, but even a short walk makes a difference. Since I started, I have felt more energetic in the afternoons.
questions.model_answer_ko: 지난 1년 동안 더 나은 습관을 만들려고 노력해 왔어요. 매일 최소 30분은 걷도록 하고, 보통 저녁 식사 후에 걸어요. 패스트푸드는 줄이고 물은 더 마시려고 해요. 회사 일로 바쁘면 계속하기 힘들지만 짧은 산책만 해도 차이가 있어요. 시작한 뒤로 오후에 더 활력이 생겼어요.

follow_ups.question: Is it difficult for you to find time for exercise?
follow_ups.sample_answer: Sometimes. I try to use the stairs and walk during lunch, so I do not need a special time.

follow_ups.question: Do you think people in your country are healthy?
follow_ups.sample_answer: Many people care about health, but long working hours make it hard to sleep and exercise enough.

follow_ups.question: What unhealthy habit would you like to change?
follow_ups.sample_answer: I drink too much coffee. I am trying to switch to tea after lunch.

questions.question: How has technology changed the way you work or live?
questions.question_ko: 기술이 당신의 일이나 생활을 어떻게 바꿨나요?

useful_phrases.text: It has made it much easier to...

questions.model_answer: Technology has made it much easier to stay in touch with people and to work from anywhere. I can't imagine life without my phone because I use it for banking, maps and translation. At work, online tools help us share documents and finish projects faster. The downside is that I am always available, so it is hard to switch off in the evening. I am trying to turn off work notifications after seven.
questions.model_answer_ko: 기술 덕분에 사람들과 연락하고 어디서든 일하기가 훨씬 쉬워졌어요. 은행 업무, 지도, 번역에 쓰기 때문에 휴대폰 없는 삶은 상상이 안 돼요. 직장에서는 온라인 도구로 문서를 공유하고 프로젝트를 더 빨리 끝내요. 단점은 항상 연락이 닿는 상태라 저녁에 끄기가 어렵다는 거예요. 저녁 7시 이후에는 업무 알림을 끄려고 노력하고 있어요.

follow_ups.question: Which app could you not live without?
follow_ups.sample_answer: My map app. I have a terrible sense of direction, so it saves me all the time.

follow_ups.question: Do you think children spend too much time on screens?
follow_ups.question_ko: 아이들이 화면을 너무 많이 본다고 생각하나요?
follow_ups.sample_answer: Yes, I do. I think parents should set clear limits and encourage outdoor play.

follow_ups.question: What new technology are you excited about?
follow_ups.sample_answer: I am excited about real-time translation. It could make travelling and business much easier.

questions.question: What is the hardest part of learning English for you?
questions.question_ko: 영어 공부에서 가장 어려운 점은 무엇인가요?

useful_phrases.text: What I find most difficult is...
I have improved a lot since I started...
One thing that works for me is...

questions.model_answer: What I find most difficult is speaking without preparing. I understand a lot when I read, but when someone asks me a question, my mind goes blank. I have improved a lot since I started practising a little every day. One thing that works for me is repeating sentences out loud and recording myself. I still make mistakes, but I am less afraid of them now.
questions.model_answer_ko: 가장 어려운 건 준비 없이 말하는 거예요. 읽을 때는 많이 이해하는데 누가 질문하면 머릿속이 하얘져요. 매일 조금씩 연습하기 시작한 뒤로 많이 늘었어요. 저에게 효과 있는 건 문장을 소리 내어 반복하고 녹음하는 거예요. 여전히 실수하지만 이제는 덜 두려워요.

follow_ups.question: How much time do you spend on English every week?
follow_ups.sample_answer: About five hours. Most of it is short sessions of 20 or 30 minutes on my commute.

follow_ups.question: Have you ever used English at work?
follow_ups.question_ko: 직장에서 영어를 써 본 적 있나요?
follow_ups.sample_answer: Yes, in emails and sometimes on calls. I still prepare a few phrases before important calls.

follow_ups.question: What advice would you give to a beginner?
follow_ups.sample_answer: Do not wait until you are perfect. Start speaking early and learn from your mistakes.

questions.question: What do you like and dislike about living in a big city?

useful_phrases.text: If I had the choice, I would...

questions.model_answer: One thing I like is that everything is nearby. There are good restaurants, public transport and lots of job opportunities. What bothers me is the noise and the crowds, especially on the subway in the morning. Also, housing is very expensive. If I had the choice, I would live in a smaller city with a park nearby, but I would still visit the capital for work.
questions.model_answer_ko: 좋은 점 하나는 모든 게 가까이에 있다는 거예요. 좋은 식당과 대중교통, 일자리 기회가 많아요. 신경 쓰이는 건 소음과 사람들, 특히 아침 지하철이에요. 또 집값이 너무 비싸요. 선택할 수 있다면 근처에 공원이 있는 더 작은 도시에 살고 싶지만 일 때문에 수도에는 계속 갈 거예요.

follow_ups.question: How do you usually get around the city?
follow_ups.sample_answer: I take the subway because it is fast and cheap. On weekends I sometimes cycle along the river.

follow_ups.question: What is your favourite place in your city?
follow_ups.sample_answer: A small park near my home. It is quiet, and I go there to read on Sundays.

follow_ups.question: Would you ever move to the countryside?
follow_ups.sample_answer: Maybe when I retire. For now, I need to stay close to my job.

questions.question: What are your habits when it comes to money?

useful_phrases.text: I try to save a part of my salary every month.
I keep track of my spending.
I tend to spend too much on...

questions.model_answer: I try to save about twenty percent of my salary every month. I keep track of my spending with an app, so I know where my money goes. I tend to spend too much on coffee and online shopping, so I set a small monthly limit. Last year I started an emergency fund, which makes me feel safer. In the future, I would like to start investing a little.
questions.model_answer_ko: 매달 월급의 20퍼센트쯤을 저축하려고 해요. 앱으로 지출을 기록해서 돈이 어디로 가는지 알아요. 커피와 온라인 쇼핑에 돈을 너무 쓰는 편이라 월 한도를 작게 정해요. 작년에 비상금을 만들었는데 마음이 더 편해요. 앞으로는 투자도 조금 시작하고 싶어요.

follow_ups.question: Do you ever buy things you do not need?
follow_ups.question_ko: 필요 없는 물건을 산 적이 있나요?
follow_ups.sample_answer: Yes, all the time! Now I wait 24 hours before I buy anything expensive.

follow_ups.question: Is it important to you to save for the future?
follow_ups.sample_answer: Very important. I do not want to worry about money when I am older.

follow_ups.question: What was the best purchase you have made?
follow_ups.sample_answer: A good pair of walking shoes. I use them every day, and they have lasted three years.

questions.question: How do you keep a good balance between work and personal life?
questions.question_ko: 일과 개인 생활의 균형을 어떻게 유지하나요?

useful_phrases.text: I try to set clear boundaries.
When I feel burned out, I...

questions.model_answer: I try to set clear boundaries between work and home. I leave the office at six unless there is an emergency, and I do not check emails after dinner. I make time for my hobbies, like cooking and hiking, at least once a week. When I feel burned out, I take a day off and do nothing special. It is not always easy, but I think rest actually makes me more productive.
questions.model_answer_ko: 일과 집 사이에 분명한 선을 정하려고 해요. 긴급 상황이 아니면 6시에 퇴근하고 저녁 식사 후에는 이메일을 확인하지 않아요. 요리나 등산 같은 취미를 위해 적어도 일주일에 한 번은 시간을 내요. 번아웃이 오면 하루 쉬면서 특별한 걸 하지 않아요. 항상 쉽지는 않지만 쉬는 게 오히려 생산성을 높인다고 생각해요.

follow_ups.question: Do you often work overtime?
follow_ups.sample_answer: Only before big deadlines, maybe twice a month. I try to take that time back later.

follow_ups.question: What do you do to relax after a stressful day?
follow_ups.question_ko: 스트레스 많은 날 뒤에는 어떻게 쉬나요?
follow_ups.sample_answer: I listen to music and take a long shower. Sometimes I call a friend.

follow_ups.question: Do you think companies should offer a four-day work week?
follow_ups.sample_answer: I think it is a great idea if the work still gets done. People would be happier and more focused.

questions.question: Would you ever change your career? Why or why not?

useful_phrases.text: If I found the right opportunity, I would...

questions.model_answer: I have been thinking about it for a while, actually. If I found the right opportunity, I would move into a more creative role, maybe in marketing. The risk is that I would have to start at a lower salary and learn many new things. On the other hand, I would be more motivated. For now, I am taking an evening course to test whether I really enjoy it.
questions.model_answer_ko: 사실 한동안 생각해 왔어요. 좋은 기회를 찾으면 더 창의적인 역할, 아마 마케팅으로 옮기고 싶어요. 위험은 더 낮은 연봉으로 시작하고 새로운 걸 많이 배워야 한다는 거예요. 반면에 동기부여는 더 될 거예요. 지금은 정말 맞는지 확인하려고 저녁 수업을 듣고 있어요.

follow_ups.question: What would make you leave your current job?
follow_ups.question_ko: 지금 직장을 떠나게 만들 요인은 무엇인가요?
follow_ups.sample_answer: If I stopped learning or if my manager did not support me, I would start looking.

follow_ups.question: Who could give you advice about this?
follow_ups.question_ko: 이 문제에 대해 누가 조언해 줄 수 있나요?
follow_ups.sample_answer: A friend who works in marketing. We are having lunch next week to talk about it.

follow_ups.question: Is salary or job satisfaction more important to you?
follow_ups.question_ko: 연봉과 직업 만족도 중 무엇이 더 중요한가요?
follow_ups.sample_answer: Satisfaction, as long as the salary is enough to live comfortably.

questions.question: Do you enjoy cooking? What do you usually make?

useful_phrases.text: I have been cooking more since...
It is a great way to relax.

questions.model_answer: Yes, I have been cooking more since I started working from home. My go-to dish is a simple vegetable stew with rice, because it is quick and healthy. On weekends, I like trying new recipes, like pasta or Thai curry. It is a great way to relax after a long week. Sometimes I fail, but my friends are kind and eat it anyway.
questions.model_answer_ko: 네, 재택근무를 시작한 뒤로 요리를 더 많이 해요. 자주 만드는 요리는 밥과 함께 먹는 간단한 채소 찌개인데 빠르고 건강하거든요. 주말에는 파스타나 태국 커리 같은 새로운 요리법을 시도하는 걸 좋아해요. 긴 한 주 뒤에 긴장을 푸는 좋은 방법이에요. 가끔 실패하지만 친구들은 착해서 그래도 먹어 줘요.

follow_ups.question: Do you prefer eating out or eating at home?
follow_ups.question_ko: 외식과 집밥 중 무엇을 더 좋아하나요?
follow_ups.sample_answer: Mostly at home because it is cheaper, but I love going out with friends on Fridays.

follow_ups.question: What is the most difficult dish you have tried?
follow_ups.question_ko: 만들어 본 가장 어려운 요리는 무엇인가요?
follow_ups.sample_answer: Homemade dumplings. It took hours, and they looked strange, but they tasted great.

follow_ups.question: Who taught you to cook?
follow_ups.sample_answer: My mother taught me the basics, and I learned the rest from online videos.

questions.question: How much time do you spend on social media, and is it a good thing?
questions.question_ko: 소셜 미디어에 시간을 얼마나 쓰나요? 좋은 일일까요?

useful_phrases.text: I spend about... a day on it.
I've decided to cut down on...

questions.model_answer: I spend about an hour a day on social media, mostly in the evening. It is useful for keeping in touch with friends and following news in my industry. But it can waste a lot of time, and sometimes I feel worse after I see other people's perfect lives. I have decided to cut down, so I deleted one app from my phone last month. So far, I have been sleeping better.
questions.model_answer_ko: 하루에 한 시간쯤, 주로 저녁에 소셜 미디어를 해요. 친구들과 연락하고 업계 소식을 보는 데는 유용해요. 하지만 시간을 많이 낭비하게 하고 남들의 완벽한 삶을 보면 기분이 나빠지기도 해요. 줄이기로 해서 지난달에 앱 하나를 휴대폰에서 지웠어요. 지금까지는 잠을 더 잘 자고 있어요.

follow_ups.question: Do you post often?
follow_ups.sample_answer: Not really. I mostly look at other people's posts and sometimes share travel photos.

follow_ups.question: Has social media affected your work?
follow_ups.sample_answer: Yes, both ways. It helped me find a mentor, but it also distracts me during the day.

follow_ups.question: Would you be able to live without it for a month?
follow_ups.question_ko: 한 달 동안 소셜 미디어 없이 살 수 있을까요?
follow_ups.sample_answer: I think so. It would be difficult at first, but I would have more time to read.

questions.question: How do you stay motivated to exercise regularly?

useful_phrases.text: It helps to have a routine.
I work out with a friend.

questions.model_answer: It helps to have a routine, so I go to the gym every Monday, Wednesday and Friday after work. I work out with a friend, which makes it harder to cancel. I also set small goals, like running five kilometres without stopping. Last month I reached that goal, and I felt really proud. When I am tired, I tell myself I only need to go for ten minutes, and usually I stay longer.
questions.model_answer_ko: 루틴이 있으면 도움이 돼서 월, 수, 금 퇴근 후에 헬스장에 가요. 친구와 함께 운동하면 취소하기가 더 어려워져요. 쉬지 않고 5킬로미터 달리기 같은 작은 목표도 세워요. 지난달에 그 목표를 이뤘고 정말 뿌듯했어요. 피곤할 때는 10분만 하자고 스스로에게 말하는데 보통은 더 오래 있게 돼요.

follow_ups.question: What sport would you like to try?
follow_ups.sample_answer: I would like to try climbing. I have heard it is great for strength and focus.

follow_ups.question: Do you prefer exercising indoors or outdoors?
follow_ups.question_ko: 실내 운동과 야외 운동 중 어느 쪽이 좋아요?
follow_ups.sample_answer: Outdoors, definitely. Fresh air makes me feel more relaxed.

follow_ups.question: What do you do when you miss a workout?
follow_ups.sample_answer: I do not feel guilty. I just go the next day and keep going.

questions.question: Describe your daily commute. Would you change anything?
questions.question_ko: 출퇴근 과정을 설명해 주세요. 바꾸고 싶은 게 있나요?

useful_phrases.text: It takes me about... to get to work.

questions.model_answer: It takes me about fifty minutes to get to work by subway and a short bus ride. I use the time to listen to English podcasts or catch up on emails. The worst part is the morning rush, when the train is so crowded that I can hardly move. If I could, I would start work an hour later to avoid it. My company is thinking about flexible hours, so I am hopeful.
questions.model_answer_ko: 지하철과 짧은 버스로 출근하는 데 약 50분 걸려요. 그 시간에 영어 팟캐스트를 듣거나 이메일을 확인해요. 최악은 아침 러시아워로 기차가 너무 붐벼서 거의 움직일 수 없어요. 할 수 있다면 그것을 피하려고 한 시간 늦게 시작하겠어요. 회사에서 유연 근무를 검토하고 있어서 기대하고 있어요.

follow_ups.question: Have you ever been late because of transport?
follow_ups.sample_answer: Yes, during a subway strike last winter. I called my manager and worked from a cafe.

follow_ups.question: Would you rather drive or take public transport?
follow_ups.sample_answer: Public transport. Driving in the city is stressful, and parking is expensive.

follow_ups.question: How could cities improve their public transport?
follow_ups.question_ko: 도시는 대중교통을 어떻게 개선할 수 있을까요?
follow_ups.sample_answer: More frequent trains at rush hour and better apps with live information would help.

questions.question: Do you prefer shopping online or in stores?
questions.question_ko: 온라인 쇼핑과 매장 쇼핑 중 무엇을 선호하나요?

useful_phrases.text: I like to see it in person first.

questions.model_answer: I mostly buy everyday things online because it is convenient and it is easy to compare prices. However, for clothes and shoes, I like to see them in person first. I once ordered a jacket online, and it did not fit, so I had to return it. That was annoying. These days I try on things in the store and then decide whether to buy there or online.
questions.model_answer_ko: 일상용품은 편리하고 가격 비교가 쉬워서 주로 온라인으로 사요. 하지만 옷과 신발은 먼저 직접 보는 걸 좋아해요. 한 번은 재킷을 온라인으로 주문했는데 안 맞아서 반품해야 했어요. 짜증 났어요. 요즘은 매장에서 입어 보고 거기서 살지 온라인으로 살지 정해요.

follow_ups.question: Have you ever received a wrong or damaged item?
follow_ups.question_ko: 잘못된 물건이나 파손된 물건을 받은 적 있나요?
follow_ups.sample_answer: Yes, a broken cup. I sent a photo to customer service, and they sent a new one.

follow_ups.question: Do reviews influence your decisions?
follow_ups.sample_answer: A lot. I always read the bad reviews first to see the problems.

follow_ups.question: What is the last thing you bought that you were happy with?
follow_ups.question_ko: 최근에 산 것 중 만족한 것은 무엇인가요?
follow_ups.sample_answer: A desk lamp. It was cheap, but it makes my workspace much nicer.

questions.question: How do you feel about using AI tools at work?
questions.question_ko: 직장에서 AI 도구를 쓰는 것에 대해 어떻게 생각하나요?

useful_phrases.text: I use it to help me with...
I am a bit worried that...

questions.model_answer: I think AI tools are very useful if you use them wisely. I use them to help me write first drafts of emails and to summarize long documents. However, I always double-check the results, because they can contain mistakes. I am a bit worried that some people will depend on them too much and stop thinking for themselves. Overall, I believe AI will save us time, so we can focus on more important work.
questions.model_answer_ko: 현명하게 쓰면 AI 도구는 매우 유용하다고 생각해요. 이메일 초안을 쓰거나 긴 문서를 요약할 때 도움을 받아요. 하지만 실수가 있을 수 있어서 항상 결과를 다시 확인해요. 어떤 사람들이 너무 의존해서 스스로 생각하지 않게 될까 봐 조금 걱정돼요. 전반적으로 AI가 시간을 아껴 줘서 더 중요한 일에 집중할 수 있을 거라고 믿어요.

follow_ups.question: Do you think AI will take away jobs?
follow_ups.sample_answer: Some jobs will change, but new ones will appear. People need to keep learning new skills.

follow_ups.question: What task would you most like AI to handle for you?
follow_ups.question_ko: AI가 대신해 줬으면 하는 일은 무엇인가요?
follow_ups.sample_answer: Scheduling meetings. It takes so much time to find a day that works for everyone.

follow_ups.question: Does your company have rules about using AI?
follow_ups.sample_answer: Yes, we must not put customer data into public tools. I think that is sensible.

questions.question: What hobby have you picked up recently?

useful_phrases.text: I'm not very good yet, but...
I would recommend it to anyone who...

questions.model_answer: I recently got into pottery. A friend invited me to a beginner class, and I loved it right away. I am not very good yet, and my first bowl looked more like a hat. But working with my hands helps me forget about work stress. I would recommend it to anyone who spends all day on a computer.
questions.model_answer_ko: 최근에 도예에 빠졌어요. 친구가 초보자 수업에 초대했는데 바로 좋아하게 됐어요. 아직 잘하진 못하고 첫 그릇은 모자처럼 생겼어요. 하지만 손으로 작업하면 업무 스트레스를 잊게 돼요. 하루 종일 컴퓨터를 보는 사람에게 추천해요.

follow_ups.question: How often do you practise it?
follow_ups.sample_answer: Once a week in class, and sometimes I go to the studio on Sunday afternoons.

follow_ups.question: Why do hobbies matter?
follow_ups.sample_answer: They give us something to enjoy that is not about money or work. That keeps me balanced.

follow_ups.question: What hobby would you like to try next?
follow_ups.sample_answer: I would like to learn the guitar. I have wanted to play since I was a teenager.

questions.question: If you wanted to buy something big, like a car or an apartment, how would you plan for it?
questions.question_ko: 자동차나 집 같은 큰 것을 사고 싶다면 어떻게 계획하겠어요?

useful_phrases.text: I would start by setting a budget.
It might take me a few years to save enough.
useful_phrases.ko: 충분히 모으려면 몇 년 걸릴 수도 있어요.

questions.model_answer: If I wanted to buy an apartment, I would start by setting a budget and checking how much I could borrow. It might take me a few years to save enough for the down payment. I would compare several areas and visit each one at different times of day. I would also talk to people who have already bought a home. Most of all, I would not rush, because it is a huge decision.
questions.model_answer_ko: 집을 사고 싶다면 예산을 정하고 얼마나 대출받을 수 있는지 확인하는 것부터 시작하겠어요. 계약금을 충분히 모으려면 몇 년 걸릴 수도 있어요. 여러 지역을 비교하고 하루 중 다른 시간대에 각각 방문해 보겠어요. 이미 집을 산 사람들과도 이야기하겠어요. 무엇보다 큰 결정이라서 서두르지 않겠어요.

follow_ups.question: Is it better to rent or to buy?
follow_ups.question_ko: 임대와 구매 중 어느 쪽이 나을까요?
follow_ups.sample_answer: It depends. Renting is more flexible, but buying can be safer in the long term.

follow_ups.question: What would you cut from your spending to save faster?
follow_ups.question_ko: 더 빨리 모으려면 어떤 지출을 줄이겠어요?
follow_ups.sample_answer: Eating out and subscriptions. I pay for three streaming services, and I only use one.

follow_ups.question: Would you borrow money from family?
follow_ups.sample_answer: Only if we agreed on clear terms. Money can cause problems in a family.

questions.question: How do you react when your boss or a colleague disagrees with your idea?
questions.question_ko: 상사나 동료가 당신의 아이디어에 반대하면 어떻게 반응하나요?

useful_phrases.text: I try not to take it personally.
Can you tell me more about your concerns?
Maybe we can find a compromise.

questions.model_answer: I try not to take it personally, because disagreement is normal at work. First, I ask, Can you tell me more about your concerns? Often they notice something I missed. If I still believe in my idea, I explain my reasons with facts and examples. If we still do not agree, maybe we can find a compromise or test a small version first. I think pushing back politely is better than staying silent.
questions.model_answer_ko: 직장에서 의견 불일치는 당연하니 개인적으로 받아들이지 않으려고 해요. 먼저 우려하는 점을 더 말씀해 주시겠어요라고 물어요. 제가 놓친 걸 알아차린 경우가 많거든요. 그래도 제 아이디어를 믿으면 사실과 예시로 이유를 설명해요. 그래도 합의가 안 되면 타협점을 찾거나 작은 버전을 먼저 시험해 볼 수 있어요. 정중하게 반대 의견을 내는 게 조용히 있는 것보다 낫다고 생각해요.

follow_ups.question: Have you ever changed your mind after a discussion?
follow_ups.question_ko: 토론 후 생각을 바꾼 적 있나요?
follow_ups.sample_answer: Yes, many times. Last month my colleague showed me data that proved my plan was too expensive.

follow_ups.question: Is it easy to disagree with your boss?
follow_ups.question_ko: 상사에게 반대 의견을 내는 게 쉬운가요?
follow_ups.sample_answer: It depends on the boss. With mine, it is fine if I am polite and prepared.

follow_ups.question: How can a manager encourage honest opinions?
follow_ups.question_ko: 관리자는 솔직한 의견을 어떻게 장려할 수 있나요?
follow_ups.sample_answer: By asking for opinions and thanking people for criticism. They must not get angry.

questions.question: How would you help a new colleague who has just joined your team?
questions.question_ko: 팀에 막 들어온 새 동료를 어떻게 도와주겠어요?

useful_phrases.text: I remember how it felt when I joined.

questions.model_answer: I remember how it felt when I joined my company, so I would try to make the person feel welcome. I would show them around the office and introduce them to the team. Then I would explain how we work and which tools we use. I would tell them, Don't hesitate to ask me anything. After a week, I would check in to see how they are doing.
questions.model_answer_ko: 제가 입사했을 때의 기분이 기억나서 새 동료가 환영받는 느낌이 들게 하려고 할 거예요. 사무실을 안내하고 팀원들에게 소개하겠어요. 그다음 우리가 어떻게 일하고 어떤 도구를 쓰는지 설명하겠어요. 무엇이든 주저하지 말고 물어보라고 말하겠어요. 일주일 뒤에는 어떻게 지내는지 확인하겠어요.

follow_ups.question: What was your first week at your current job like?
follow_ups.sample_answer: It was busy. I met many people, but I forgot most of their names!

follow_ups.question: What information is most useful for a new employee?
follow_ups.sample_answer: Who to ask for what. Knowing the right person saves a lot of time.

follow_ups.question: Do you think a buddy system works?
follow_ups.sample_answer: Yes. New people feel less afraid to ask simple questions.

questions.question: How much sleep do you get, and how does it affect your day?
questions.question_ko: 잠을 얼마나 자고, 하루에 어떤 영향을 주나요?

useful_phrases.text: I usually get about... hours of sleep.
When I don't sleep well, I...
I've started going to bed earlier.

questions.model_answer: I usually get about six hours of sleep, which is not enough. When I don't sleep well, I find it hard to concentrate, and I get irritated easily. I have started going to bed earlier and putting my phone in another room. I also stopped drinking coffee after three in the afternoon. After two weeks, I already feel more awake in the morning.
questions.model_answer_ko: 보통 여섯 시간쯤 자는데 충분하지 않아요. 잠을 잘 못 자면 집중하기 어렵고 쉽게 짜증이 나요. 더 일찍 자기 시작했고 휴대폰을 다른 방에 두고 있어요. 오후 3시 이후에는 커피도 끊었어요. 2주가 지났는데 벌써 아침에 더 말똥말똥해요.

follow_ups.question: Do you take naps?
follow_ups.sample_answer: On weekends, sometimes for twenty minutes. Any longer and I feel worse.

follow_ups.question: What keeps you awake at night?
follow_ups.question_ko: 밤에 잠 못 들게 하는 것은 무엇인가요?
follow_ups.sample_answer: Usually work thoughts. Writing a to-do list before bed helps a lot.

follow_ups.question: Do you think people should start work later?
follow_ups.question_ko: 사람들이 일을 더 늦게 시작해야 한다고 생각하나요?
follow_ups.sample_answer: Yes, I do. Many people work better in the late morning.

questions.question: Would you like to live or work in another country? Why?
questions.question_ko: 다른 나라에서 살거나 일하고 싶나요? 이유는요?

useful_phrases.text: It would be a great way to...

questions.model_answer: I would love to work abroad for a year or two. It would be a great way to improve my English and to learn a different working culture. The biggest challenge would be missing my family and friends. I would also need to deal with paperwork and finding a place to live. Still, I think I would grow a lot as a person, so I would take the chance if it came up.
questions.model_answer_ko: 1~2년쯤 해외에서 일하고 싶어요. 영어를 늘리고 다른 업무 문화를 배우는 좋은 방법일 거예요. 가장 큰 어려움은 가족과 친구들이 그리운 거예요. 서류 작업과 살 곳 찾는 것도 해결해야 해요. 그래도 사람으로서 많이 성장할 것 같아서 기회가 오면 잡겠어요.

follow_ups.question: Which country would you choose?
follow_ups.sample_answer: Canada, because it is friendly to foreigners and I could practise English every day.

follow_ups.question: What would you miss most from home?
follow_ups.sample_answer: Definitely the food, and my family.

follow_ups.question: How would you prepare for the move?
follow_ups.sample_answer: I would study the local rules, save some extra money and make a list of useful phrases.

questions.question: What is the best way to give feedback to a colleague?
questions.question_ko: 동료에게 피드백을 주는 가장 좋은 방법은 무엇인가요?

useful_phrases.text: I would start with something positive.

questions.model_answer: I think the best way is to do it privately and kindly. I would start with something positive, so the person does not feel attacked. Then I would be specific and give examples, instead of saying something general like, You are careless. I'd suggest trying a different approach and ask what they think. Finally, I would offer my help if they need it.
questions.model_answer_ko: 비공개로, 그리고 친절하게 하는 게 최선이라고 생각해요. 공격받는 느낌이 들지 않게 긍정적인 말로 시작하겠어요. 그다음 당신은 부주의해요 같은 일반적인 말 대신 구체적인 예를 들겠어요. 다른 접근을 시도해 보라고 제안하고 어떻게 생각하는지 물어보겠어요. 마지막으로 필요하면 도와주겠다고 하겠어요.

follow_ups.question: How do you feel when you receive criticism?
follow_ups.sample_answer: At first I feel uncomfortable, but later I usually realize it helped me.

follow_ups.question: Have you ever given feedback that went badly?
follow_ups.sample_answer: Yes, I was too direct once. Now I think about my tone before I speak.

follow_ups.question: How often should managers give feedback?
follow_ups.question_ko: 관리자는 얼마나 자주 피드백을 줘야 할까요?
follow_ups.sample_answer: Regularly, not just once a year. Small comments are easier to hear.

questions.question: Tell me about a mistake you made at work and what you learned.
questions.question_ko: 직장에서 한 실수와 거기서 배운 것을 말해 주세요.
questions.model_answer: Two years ago I made the mistake of sending a price list to the wrong client by email. I realized it immediately and told my manager. I took responsibility, called the client and asked them to delete the file. Fortunately, the client was understanding. Since then, I always double-check the recipient before I click send.
questions.model_answer_ko: 2년 전에 가격표를 잘못된 고객에게 이메일로 보내는 실수를 했어요. 바로 알아차리고 매니저에게 말했어요. 책임을 지고 고객에게 전화해서 파일을 삭제해 달라고 부탁했어요. 다행히 고객이 이해해 줬어요. 그 이후로 저는 보내기를 누르기 전에 항상 수신자를 다시 확인해요.

follow_ups.question: How did you feel at that moment?
follow_ups.sample_answer: Terrible. My heart was racing, but being honest made me feel better.

follow_ups.question: Is it okay to make mistakes at work?
follow_ups.sample_answer: Yes, if you learn from them and tell people early.

follow_ups.question: How does your company handle mistakes?
follow_ups.sample_answer: We have a short review where we ask what happened and how to prevent it, not who is guilty.

questions.question: What do you think makes a leader truly effective, as opposed to merely senior?
questions.question_ko: 단지 직급만 높은 사람이 아니라 진정으로 효과적인 리더는 무엇이 다르다고 생각하세요?

useful_phrases.text: I'd argue that the real test of leadership is...
It seems to me that seniority and influence are two different things.
What sets great leaders apart is their ability to...
useful_phrases.ko: 훌륭한 리더를 구별 짓는 건 ...하는 능력이에요.

questions.model_answer: I'd argue that the real test of leadership is what happens when you're not in the room. A merely senior person gets compliance because of their title, whereas an effective leader builds a team that makes good decisions independently. It seems to me that this comes down to trust and clarity: people need to know what the goal is and why it matters. The best manager I ever had rarely gave orders. Instead, she asked sharp questions and let us find the answers ourselves. As a result, we took ownership, and the results spoke for themselves.
questions.model_answer_ko: 리더십의 진짜 시험대는 내가 그 자리에 없을 때 무슨 일이 일어나느냐라고 생각해요. 직급만 높은 사람은 직함 덕분에 따르게 만들지만, 효과적인 리더는 스스로 좋은 결정을 내리는 팀을 만들어요. 제가 보기엔 이건 신뢰와 명확성의 문제예요. 사람들은 목표가 무엇이고 왜 중요한지 알아야 하거든요. 제가 만난 최고의 상사는 좀처럼 명령하지 않았어요. 대신 날카로운 질문을 던지고 우리가 답을 직접 찾게 했죠. 그 덕분에 우리는 주인의식을 가졌고 결과가 모든 걸 말해 줬어요.

follow_ups.question: Can leadership be taught, or is it mostly a matter of personality?
follow_ups.question_ko: 리더십은 가르칠 수 있을까요, 아니면 대부분 성격 문제일까요?
follow_ups.sample_answer: I think the fundamentals can definitely be taught, such as giving feedback and running meetings. Personality does shape your style, though. The key is self-awareness, which people can develop over time.

follow_ups.question: How do you lead people who are more experienced than you?
follow_ups.question_ko: 자신보다 경험이 많은 사람들은 어떻게 이끄세요?
follow_ups.sample_answer: I try to be upfront that I'm not the expert in the room. I focus on removing obstacles and asking for their input. In my experience, respect follows when you genuinely value their expertise.

follow_ups.question: Have you ever had to lead through a difficult change?
follow_ups.question_ko: 어려운 변화를 이끌어 본 적이 있나요?
follow_ups.sample_answer: Yes, when our department was restructured last year. I was transparent about what I knew and didn't know. That honesty kept morale from collapsing, even though the process was painful.

questions.question: How do you approach a conflict with a colleague who sees things very differently?
questions.question_ko: 의견이 크게 다른 동료와의 갈등에는 어떻게 접근하나요?

useful_phrases.text: My first instinct is to try to understand where they're coming from.
useful_phrases.ko: 제 첫 본능은 상대의 입장을 이해해 보는 거예요.

useful_phrases.text: Rather than taking sides, I try to focus on the underlying interests.
useful_phrases.ko: 편을 가르기보다 근본적인 이해관계에 집중하려 해요.

useful_phrases.text: In the end, we found some common ground.

questions.model_answer: My first instinct is to have a private conversation rather than let tension build up. I try to listen properly before I defend my own position, because quite often the disagreement turns out to be about priorities rather than personalities. Once I understand their underlying concern, it's much easier to look for common ground. If we still can't agree, I'd suggest involving a neutral third party, such as our manager, to help us decide. What matters most is that we keep the relationship intact, since we'll have to work together long after this issue is forgotten.
questions.model_answer_ko: 저는 긴장이 쌓이게 두기보다 먼저 일대일로 조용히 대화하려고 해요. 제 입장을 방어하기 전에 제대로 듣는데, 갈등이 성격 문제가 아니라 우선순위 문제인 경우가 꽤 많거든요. 상대의 근본적인 걱정을 이해하면 공통분모를 찾기가 훨씬 쉬워져요. 그래도 합의가 안 되면 매니저 같은 중립적인 제3자를 끌어들이자고 제안할 거예요. 가장 중요한 건 관계를 지키는 거예요. 이 문제가 잊힌 뒤에도 계속 함께 일해야 하니까요.

follow_ups.question: Is there such a thing as healthy conflict at work?
follow_ups.sample_answer: Absolutely. Constructive disagreement often leads to better decisions, because it forces people to test their assumptions. The problem starts when it becomes personal.

follow_ups.question: What do you do if the other person refuses to talk?
follow_ups.sample_answer: I'd give them some space and try again later in a more informal setting. If that fails, I'd escalate, but only after making it clear to them that I'm doing so.

follow_ups.question: Can you describe a conflict that you handled badly?
follow_ups.question_ko: 잘못 대처했던 갈등 사례를 말해 줄 수 있나요?
follow_ups.sample_answer: Early in my career, I sent a sharp email instead of picking up the phone. It made things worse. Since then, I've always raised sensitive issues face to face.

questions.question: How should a company decide when to say no to a profitable opportunity?
questions.question_ko: 회사는 수익성 있는 기회를 언제 거절해야 한다고 생각하세요?

useful_phrases.text: Strategy is as much about what you decline as what you pursue.
useful_phrases.ko: 전략은 추구하는 것만큼 거절하는 것에 달려 있어요.

useful_phrases.text: It might be profitable in the short term, but it could distract us from our core business.
useful_phrases.ko: 단기적으로는 수익이 나도 핵심 사업에서 주의를 흩뜨릴 수 있어요.

useful_phrases.text: The opportunity cost can be considerable.

questions.model_answer: I'd say strategy is as much about what you decline as what you pursue. A deal can look profitable on paper and still pull a company away from its core strengths. When I evaluate an opportunity, I ask three questions: does it fit our long-term direction, do we have the capacity to deliver it well, and what would we have to give up? The opportunity cost can be considerable, especially for a small team. I'd also be wary of customers who demand heavy customization, because that can quietly turn a product company into a consultancy. Saying no politely, and explaining why, usually preserves the relationship.
questions.model_answer_ko: 전략은 추구하는 것만큼 거절하는 것에 달려 있다고 생각해요. 서류상으로는 수익성이 좋아 보여도 회사를 핵심 강점에서 멀어지게 할 수 있거든요. 기회를 평가할 때 저는 세 가지를 물어요. 우리의 장기 방향과 맞는지, 잘 해낼 역량이 있는지, 그러려면 무엇을 포기해야 하는지요. 특히 작은 팀에는 기회비용이 상당할 수 있어요. 과도한 맞춤화를 요구하는 고객도 경계하는데, 그러면 제품 회사가 어느새 컨설팅 회사로 변할 수 있기 때문이에요. 정중하게 거절하고 이유를 설명하면 보통 관계도 유지돼요.

follow_ups.question: Have you ever regretted turning something down?
follow_ups.sample_answer: Once or twice, yes. But on balance, the focus we gained was worth it. I'd rather regret a missed opportunity than a failed distraction.

follow_ups.question: Who should make that call, leadership or the team?
follow_ups.question_ko: 그 결정은 리더십이 해야 할까요, 팀이 해야 할까요?
follow_ups.sample_answer: Ideally both. Leadership sets the criteria, but the team often sees the practical risks first. A shared framework avoids a lot of arguments.

follow_ups.question: How do you say no without damaging the relationship?
follow_ups.question_ko: 관계를 해치지 않고 거절하려면 어떻게 하나요?
follow_ups.sample_answer: I explain my reasoning honestly and offer an alternative, like a referral or a later start date. People usually respect a clear answer more than a vague maybe.

questions.question: What is your view on using AI tools in everyday professional work?
questions.question_ko: 일상 업무에서 AI 도구를 쓰는 것에 대해 어떻게 생각하세요?

useful_phrases.text: On the whole, I see AI as a powerful assistant rather than a replacement.
useful_phrases.ko: 대체로 AI는 대체재가 아니라 강력한 보조 도구라고 봐요.

useful_phrases.text: We need to be careful not to rely on it blindly.
It frees up time for higher-value work.
useful_phrases.ko: 더 가치 있는 일에 쓸 시간을 확보해 줘요.

questions.model_answer: On the whole, I see AI as a powerful assistant rather than a replacement. I use it to draft emails, summarize long documents, and brainstorm ideas, which frees up time for work that requires judgment. That said, we need to be careful not to rely on it blindly, because it can produce confident-sounding mistakes. I always verify facts and figures before they go into anything official. I also think companies should set clear guidelines about confidential data. Used thoughtfully, AI can raise our productivity, but accountability still rests with the person who signs off on the work.
questions.model_answer_ko: 대체로 AI는 대체재가 아니라 강력한 보조 도구라고 봐요. 저는 이메일 초안, 긴 문서 요약, 아이디어 브레인스토밍에 쓰는데, 덕분에 판단이 필요한 일에 쓸 시간이 생겨요. 다만 자신 있게 들리는 오류를 만들 수 있어서 맹목적으로 의존하지 않도록 조심해야 해요. 공식 문서에 들어가는 사실과 수치는 항상 검증해요. 기밀 데이터에 대한 명확한 지침도 회사가 정해야 한다고 생각하고요. 신중하게 쓰면 생산성을 높일 수 있지만, 결과물에 대한 책임은 여전히 승인하는 사람에게 있어요.

follow_ups.question: Do you worry about AI taking over your job?
follow_ups.question_ko: AI가 당신의 일자리를 대체할까 봐 걱정되나요?
follow_ups.sample_answer: Not entirely, but I think my role will change. The tasks that are repetitive will be automated, so I'm focusing on skills like negotiation and strategic thinking.

follow_ups.question: What risks should companies be most concerned about?
follow_ups.question_ko: 회사들이 가장 우려해야 할 위험은 무엇일까요?
follow_ups.sample_answer: Data privacy and over-reliance, I'd say. If employees stop thinking critically, errors can spread quickly and unnoticed.

follow_ups.question: How would you train a team to use AI responsibly?
follow_ups.question_ko: 팀이 AI를 책임감 있게 쓰도록 어떻게 교육하시겠어요?
follow_ups.sample_answer: I'd start with practical examples of what works and what fails. Then I'd set simple rules, such as never pasting client data into public tools and always checking the output.

questions.question: How do you manage stakeholders who have competing priorities?
questions.question_ko: 우선순위가 서로 충돌하는 이해관계자들은 어떻게 관리하나요?

useful_phrases.text: The first step is to make the trade-offs visible.
useful_phrases.ko: 첫 단계는 트레이드오프를 눈에 보이게 하는 거예요.

useful_phrases.text: I try to align everyone around a shared objective.
useful_phrases.ko: 모두를 공동의 목표 아래 정렬시키려 해요.

useful_phrases.text: I keep them in the loop so there are no surprises.
useful_phrases.ko: 놀라는 일이 없도록 계속 상황을 공유해요.

questions.model_answer: The first step is to make the trade-offs visible. When two stakeholders each want their project delivered first, I bring them together and show what the resources can realistically support. Rather than deciding behind closed doors, I try to align everyone around a shared objective, such as company revenue or customer satisfaction. If they still disagree, I escalate to a sponsor who can set the priority. Throughout the process, I keep everyone in the loop so there are no surprises. People can accept a decision they dislike, but they rarely forgive being blindsided.
questions.model_answer_ko: 첫 단계는 트레이드오프를 눈에 보이게 하는 거예요. 두 이해관계자가 각자 자기 프로젝트를 먼저 원하면, 둘을 모아 놓고 현재 자원으로 현실적으로 무엇이 가능한지 보여 줘요. 밀실에서 결정하기보다 회사 매출이나 고객 만족 같은 공동의 목표 아래 모두를 정렬시키려 하고요. 그래도 의견이 갈리면 우선순위를 정할 수 있는 후원자에게 올려요. 과정 내내 놀라는 일이 없도록 모두에게 상황을 공유해요. 사람들은 마음에 안 드는 결정은 받아들일 수 있어도 허를 찔리는 건 좀처럼 용서하지 않거든요.

follow_ups.question: What do you do when a senior stakeholder pushes unreasonable demands?
follow_ups.question_ko: 고위 이해관계자가 무리한 요구를 하면 어떻게 하세요?
follow_ups.sample_answer: I'd acknowledge the goal behind the request, then show the cost in time and quality. Putting numbers on the table usually turns an emotional demand into a practical discussion.

follow_ups.question: How often should you update stakeholders?
follow_ups.sample_answer: It depends on the stakes, but I prefer short, regular updates over long reports. A weekly summary is enough in most cases, with an immediate alert if there's a risk.

follow_ups.question: Have you ever lost a stakeholder's trust?
follow_ups.sample_answer: Yes, once, when I missed a deadline without warning them. I rebuilt trust by being transparent and by delivering small promises consistently.

questions.question: What qualities do you look for when hiring someone for your team?
questions.question_ko: 팀에 사람을 뽑을 때 어떤 자질을 보시나요?

useful_phrases.text: I tend to prioritize attitude and learning ability over specific experience.
useful_phrases.ko: 특정 경력보다 태도와 학습 능력을 우선하는 편이에요.

useful_phrases.text: I look for evidence of how they handle setbacks.
useful_phrases.ko: 좌절을 어떻게 다루는지에 대한 증거를 살펴봐요.

useful_phrases.text: A strong candidate will ask thoughtful questions.
useful_phrases.ko: 훌륭한 지원자는 생각 깊은 질문을 해요.

questions.model_answer: I tend to prioritize attitude and learning ability over specific experience, because skills can be taught while curiosity and integrity are much harder to instil. In interviews, I look for evidence of how candidates handle setbacks, so I ask them to walk me through a project that went wrong. A strong candidate will also ask thoughtful questions about the team and its challenges. I'm wary of anyone who takes all the credit and blames others for failures. Finally, I consider how someone would complement the existing team, rather than simply hiring people who think the way I do.
questions.model_answer_ko: 특정 경력보다 태도와 학습 능력을 우선하는 편이에요. 기술은 가르칠 수 있지만 호기심과 정직함은 심어 주기가 훨씬 어렵거든요. 면접에서는 좌절을 어떻게 다루는지 보려고 잘못된 프로젝트를 설명해 달라고 해요. 훌륭한 지원자는 팀과 팀의 과제에 대해 생각 깊은 질문도 하고요. 공은 다 가져가고 실패는 남 탓하는 사람은 경계해요. 마지막으로 저와 비슷하게 생각하는 사람만 뽑기보다 기존 팀을 보완할 사람인지 고려해요.

follow_ups.question: Do you trust gut feeling in hiring decisions?
follow_ups.sample_answer: I take it into account, but I try to test it against structured criteria. Gut feeling can easily reflect bias, so I'd rather use it as a prompt for further questions.

follow_ups.question: How important is cultural fit?
follow_ups.sample_answer: Shared values matter, but 'fit' can become an excuse for hiring clones. I'd rather look for people who add something new while respecting how we work.

follow_ups.question: What's the biggest hiring mistake you've seen?
follow_ups.sample_answer: Hiring in a hurry. A team once filled a role in two weeks to relieve pressure, and it took a year to correct the mismatch.

questions.question: How do you maintain a healthy work-life balance during a demanding period?
questions.question_ko: 업무가 몰리는 시기에 워라밸을 어떻게 유지하나요?

useful_phrases.text: I try to set firm boundaries, even when things get hectic.
useful_phrases.ko: 정신없을 때도 확실한 경계를 정하려 해요.

useful_phrases.text: It's about energy management rather than time management.
Burning out helps nobody in the long run.
useful_phrases.ko: 번아웃은 장기적으로 누구에게도 도움이 안 돼요.

questions.model_answer: I try to set firm boundaries, even when things get hectic. For example, I block out time for exercise and dinner with my family, and I treat those appointments like client meetings. I think it's about energy management rather than time management: a rested person does in two hours what an exhausted one does in four. During crunch periods, I also negotiate with my manager about what can wait. Burning out helps nobody in the long run, including the company. Of course, there are weeks when balance simply isn't possible, but I make sure to recover afterwards.
questions.model_answer_ko: 정신없을 때도 확실한 경계를 정하려 해요. 예를 들어 운동 시간과 가족과의 저녁 식사를 따로 확보하고, 그 일정을 고객 미팅처럼 대해요. 시간 관리보다 에너지 관리의 문제라고 생각해요. 쉰 사람이 두 시간에 할 일을 지친 사람은 네 시간이 걸리거든요. 바쁜 시기에는 매니저와 무엇을 미룰 수 있는지도 협의해요. 번아웃은 회사를 포함해 장기적으로 누구에게도 도움이 안 돼요. 물론 균형이 불가능한 주도 있지만, 그 뒤에는 꼭 회복하도록 해요.

follow_ups.question: Do you think remote work has improved or damaged work-life balance?
follow_ups.sample_answer: Both, really. It saves commuting time, but the boundary between home and work has blurred. It depends on whether people have the discipline to log off.

follow_ups.question: What responsibility do managers have here?
follow_ups.sample_answer: A big one. If a manager sends emails at midnight, the team will feel they must reply. Leaders have to model the behaviour they expect.

follow_ups.question: Is a perfect balance realistic?
follow_ups.sample_answer: Probably not. I think of it as a balance over months rather than days, with some intense periods offset by quieter ones.

questions.question: Tell me about a professional failure and what it taught you.
questions.question_ko: 직업상의 실패 경험과 그로부터 배운 점을 말해 주세요.

useful_phrases.text: The key lesson I took away was...
It was a humbling experience, but a valuable one.

questions.model_answer: A few years ago, I led a product launch that missed its target by almost forty percent. Looking back, I underestimated how much the sales team needed to be involved early on, and I assumed that a good product would sell itself. The key lesson I took away was that communication across departments is just as important as the quality of the work. After that, I started holding cross-functional reviews from the very first month. It was a humbling experience, but a valuable one. I'd argue that I learned more from that failure than from any of my successes.
questions.model_answer_ko: 몇 년 전 제품 출시를 이끌었는데 목표를 거의 40퍼센트나 놓쳤어요. 돌이켜보면 영업팀이 초기부터 참여해야 한다는 점을 과소평가했고, 좋은 제품은 저절로 팔릴 거라고 가정했어요. 제가 얻은 핵심 교훈은 부서 간 소통이 일의 품질만큼 중요하다는 거였어요. 그 뒤로는 첫 달부터 부서 간 검토 회의를 열었어요. 겸손해지는 경험이었지만 값진 경험이었어요. 어떤 성공보다 그 실패에서 더 많이 배웠다고 생각해요.

follow_ups.question: How did your team react to the failure?
follow_ups.sample_answer: Initially there was frustration, but we held an honest review without blame. That openness actually strengthened the team.

follow_ups.question: What would you do differently now?
follow_ups.sample_answer: I'd test the assumptions with real customers much earlier. A small pilot would have exposed the problem at a fraction of the cost.

follow_ups.question: Should companies reward people for taking risks that fail?
follow_ups.question_ko: 실패한 위험 감수에 회사가 보상해야 할까요?
follow_ups.sample_answer: Not the failure itself, but the quality of the thinking behind it. If people fear punishment, they will stop proposing bold ideas.

questions.question: What is the most effective way to negotiate when you have less leverage than the other side?
questions.question_ko: 상대보다 협상력이 약할 때 가장 효과적인 협상 방법은 무엇일까요?

useful_phrases.text: I'd try to identify what the other side genuinely needs.
useful_phrases.ko: 상대가 진짜 필요로 하는 것을 파악하려 할 거예요.

useful_phrases.text: It's worth knowing your best alternative in advance.
useful_phrases.ko: 미리 최선의 대안을 알아 두는 게 좋아요.

questions.model_answer: I'd say preparation is the great equalizer. If I know my alternatives and the other side's constraints better than they know mine, I'm in a stronger position than the numbers suggest. I'd try to identify what they genuinely need, which is often something other than the headline price, such as speed, reliability, or a reference customer. It's also worth knowing your walk-away point in advance so you don't agree to something out of pressure. Finally, I'd look for creative trades, offering something cheap for me but valuable to them. Even with limited leverage, a good deal is usually possible if both sides feel respected.
questions.model_answer_ko: 준비가 최고의 평형추라고 생각해요. 제 대안과 상대의 제약을 상대가 제 사정을 아는 것보다 더 잘 알면 숫자가 보여 주는 것보다 유리한 위치에 설 수 있어요. 저는 상대가 진짜 필요로 하는 걸 파악하려 할 텐데, 그건 가격 외에 속도, 신뢰성, 레퍼런스 고객 같은 경우가 많아요. 압박에 못 이겨 동의하지 않도록 포기 한계선을 미리 아는 것도 중요해요. 마지막으로 저에게는 부담이 적지만 상대에게는 가치 있는 걸 내주는 창의적인 교환을 찾겠어요. 협상력이 약해도 양쪽이 존중받는다고 느끼면 대체로 좋은 합의가 가능해요.

follow_ups.question: When should you walk away from a negotiation?
follow_ups.sample_answer: When the deal is worse than your alternative, or when the other side acts in bad faith. Walking away is only credible if you've prepared a real alternative.

follow_ups.question: Is it wise to make the first offer?
follow_ups.sample_answer: Usually, yes, because it anchors the discussion. But only if I've done enough research to make a realistic number.

follow_ups.question: How do you handle aggressive negotiators?
follow_ups.sample_answer: I stay calm and keep returning to the facts. Aggression loses much of its effect when you don't respond in kind.

questions.question: How do you decide what to prioritize when everything seems urgent?
questions.question_ko: 모든 게 급해 보일 때 무엇을 우선할지 어떻게 정하나요?

useful_phrases.text: I try to separate what's urgent from what's important.
useful_phrases.ko: 급한 것과 중요한 것을 구분하려 해요.

useful_phrases.text: I ask what the consequences of delay would be.
I'm not afraid to push back when the workload is unrealistic.

questions.model_answer: I try to separate what's urgent from what's important, because in my experience they're often confused. I ask what the consequences of delay would be: if a task has a hard deadline or affects a customer directly, it goes first. For everything else, I weigh the impact against the effort required. When I'm genuinely overloaded, I'm not afraid to push back and ask my manager which items they would rank highest. It's far better to be honest early than to promise everything and deliver nothing. At the end of each day, I also write down the top three priorities for tomorrow, which keeps me focused.
questions.model_answer_ko: 급한 것과 중요한 것을 구분하려 해요. 경험상 둘은 자주 혼동되거든요. 미루면 어떤 결과가 생기는지 물어보고, 확실한 마감이 있거나 고객에게 직접 영향을 주는 일을 먼저 해요. 나머지는 영향도와 필요한 노력을 따져 봐요. 정말 과부하일 때는 주저 없이 반대하고 매니저에게 어떤 항목이 가장 중요한지 물어봐요. 모든 걸 약속하고 아무것도 못 해내는 것보다 일찍 솔직해지는 게 훨씬 나아요. 매일 퇴근 전에 내일의 우선순위 세 가지를 적어 두는데, 그러면 집중이 유지돼요.

follow_ups.question: What tools or habits help you stay organized?
follow_ups.question_ko: 정리된 상태를 유지하는 데 도움이 되는 도구나 습관이 있나요?
follow_ups.sample_answer: A simple task list and a weekly review. I find that complicated systems tend to collapse when I'm busy.

follow_ups.question: How do you say no to a request from your boss?
follow_ups.sample_answer: I rarely say a flat no. I'd explain what I'm currently working on and ask which one should take priority.

follow_ups.question: Does constant urgency say something about company culture?
follow_ups.question_ko: 끊임없는 긴급함은 회사 문화에 대해 무엇을 말해 줄까요?
follow_ups.sample_answer: I think so. It often points to poor planning or unclear strategy. Companies that treat everything as an emergency usually burn their people out.

questions.question: How would you give difficult feedback to a high-performing but arrogant colleague?
questions.question_ko: 성과는 뛰어나지만 거만한 동료에게 어려운 피드백을 어떻게 주겠어요?

useful_phrases.text: I'd be specific about the behaviour, not the person.
useful_phrases.ko: 사람이 아니라 구체적인 행동에 대해 이야기할 거예요.

useful_phrases.text: I'd acknowledge their strengths before raising the concern.
useful_phrases.ko: 우려를 꺼내기 전에 강점을 인정할 거예요.

useful_phrases.text: I'd explain the impact their behaviour has on the team.
useful_phrases.ko: 그 행동이 팀에 미치는 영향을 설명할 거예요.

questions.model_answer: I'd start by acknowledging their strengths, because high performers usually respond better when they feel respected. Then I'd be specific about the behaviour rather than attacking the person, for instance, pointing out that interrupting colleagues in meetings has made others reluctant to speak. I'd explain the impact on the team and on their own career, since collaboration matters for promotion. After that, I'd invite their perspective, as they may not be aware of how they come across. Finally, I'd agree on a concrete next step and follow up in a few weeks to show that I take it seriously.
questions.model_answer_ko: 먼저 강점을 인정하며 시작할 거예요. 성과가 높은 사람은 존중받는다고 느낄 때 더 잘 받아들이거든요. 그다음 사람을 공격하기보다 구체적인 행동을 짚을 거예요. 예를 들어 회의에서 동료의 말을 끊어서 다른 사람들이 발언을 꺼리게 됐다고요. 팀과 본인 커리어에 미치는 영향도 설명할 텐데, 승진에는 협업이 중요하니까요. 그러고 나서 상대의 관점을 물어볼 거예요. 본인이 어떻게 보이는지 모를 수 있으니까요. 마지막으로 구체적인 다음 단계에 합의하고 몇 주 뒤에 확인해서 제가 진지하게 보고 있음을 보여 줄 거예요.

follow_ups.question: What if they get defensive?
follow_ups.sample_answer: I'd stay calm and not argue about intent. I'd say I believe they don't mean harm, but the effect is real, and then give them time to reflect.

follow_ups.question: Is it ever right to tolerate bad behaviour from a top performer?
follow_ups.question_ko: 최고 성과자의 나쁜 행동을 용인하는 게 옳을 때도 있나요?
follow_ups.sample_answer: I don't think so. Tolerating it sends the message that results excuse everything, and the rest of the team pays for it.

follow_ups.question: How do you prepare for a feedback conversation?
follow_ups.sample_answer: I write down two or three concrete examples and the outcome I'd like to see. That keeps the conversation factual instead of emotional.

questions.question: Do you think remote work is here to stay, and how has it changed company culture?
questions.question_ko: 원격 근무는 계속 이어질 것이라고 보나요? 회사 문화는 어떻게 바뀌었나요?

useful_phrases.text: On balance, I think hybrid models will prevail.
useful_phrases.ko: 종합하면 하이브리드 모델이 주류가 될 것 같아요.

useful_phrases.text: The trade-off is between flexibility and spontaneous collaboration.
useful_phrases.ko: 유연성과 즉흥적 협업 사이의 트레이드오프가 있어요.

useful_phrases.text: Culture has to be built more deliberately now.
useful_phrases.ko: 이제 문화는 더 의도적으로 만들어야 해요.

questions.model_answer: On balance, I think hybrid models will prevail, because most people value flexibility but still want some face-to-face contact. The trade-off is between flexibility and spontaneous collaboration: you lose those casual corridor conversations where ideas often start. As a result, culture has to be built more deliberately now, through clear communication norms and regular in-person gatherings. I've also noticed that remote work has shifted the focus from hours spent at a desk to actual outcomes, which I think is healthy. However, it can disadvantage junior employees who learn mostly by observation, so companies need to support them actively.
questions.model_answer_ko: 종합하면 하이브리드 모델이 주류가 될 것 같아요. 대부분의 사람이 유연성을 중요하게 여기면서도 어느 정도 대면 접촉은 원하니까요. 유연성과 즉흥적 협업 사이에 트레이드오프가 있어요. 아이디어가 시작되곤 하는 복도의 가벼운 대화를 잃게 되죠. 그래서 이제 문화는 명확한 소통 규범과 정기적인 대면 모임으로 더 의도적으로 만들어야 해요. 원격 근무가 책상 앞에 앉아 있는 시간에서 실제 성과로 초점을 옮긴 것도 건강한 변화라고 봐요. 다만 주로 관찰로 배우는 주니어 직원에게는 불리할 수 있어서 회사가 적극적으로 지원해야 해요.

follow_ups.question: Would you prefer to work fully remotely?
follow_ups.sample_answer: Not entirely. I'm most productive working from home for focused tasks, but I miss the energy of the office a couple of days a week.

follow_ups.question: How can managers keep remote teams connected?
follow_ups.question_ko: 매니저는 원격 팀의 유대를 어떻게 유지할 수 있을까요?
follow_ups.sample_answer: Through regular one-to-ones and meetings with a clear purpose. Small rituals, like a weekly informal catch-up, also help a lot.

follow_ups.question: Are there jobs that simply can't be done remotely?
follow_ups.question_ko: 원격으로는 도저히 할 수 없는 직업도 있을까요?
follow_ups.sample_answer: Of course, anything hands-on such as healthcare or manufacturing. But even there, administrative and planning tasks are becoming more flexible.

questions.question: What does corporate social responsibility mean to you, and is it more than marketing?
questions.question_ko: 기업의 사회적 책임은 당신에게 어떤 의미이며, 마케팅 그 이상일까요?

useful_phrases.text: It depends on whether the commitment is backed by action.
useful_phrases.ko: 그 약속이 행동으로 뒷받침되는지에 달려 있어요.

useful_phrases.text: There's a fine line between genuine commitment and greenwashing.
useful_phrases.ko: 진정한 약속과 그린워싱 사이의 경계는 미묘해요.

useful_phrases.text: Companies ought to be held accountable for their claims.
useful_phrases.ko: 기업은 자신들의 주장에 책임을 져야 해요.

questions.model_answer: It depends on whether the commitment is backed by action. There's a fine line between genuine commitment and a marketing exercise, and customers have become quite good at spotting the difference. For me, real responsibility means changing how the business operates, such as reducing emissions in the supply chain or paying fair wages, rather than just sponsoring a charity event. Companies ought to be held accountable for their claims, ideally through transparent reporting. That said, I don't think it's cynical if a company benefits from doing good. If it's profitable, it's more likely to last.
questions.model_answer_ko: 그 약속이 행동으로 뒷받침되는지에 달려 있어요. 진정한 약속과 마케팅 활동 사이의 경계는 미묘한데, 고객들은 그 차이를 꽤 잘 알아봐요. 제게 진짜 책임이란 자선 행사 후원이 아니라 공급망의 배출량을 줄이거나 공정한 임금을 지급하는 것처럼 사업 운영 방식을 바꾸는 거예요. 기업은 자신들의 주장에 책임을 져야 하고, 이상적으로는 투명한 보고를 통해서요. 다만 선한 일을 하면서 이익을 얻는 게 냉소적이라고는 생각하지 않아요. 수익이 나야 오래 지속될 가능성이 크니까요.

follow_ups.question: Would you choose an employer partly for its values?
follow_ups.question_ko: 가치관을 보고 직장을 선택할 수 있나요?
follow_ups.sample_answer: Yes, to a degree. If the pay and role are comparable, values would tip the balance for me.

follow_ups.question: Should governments regulate this more strictly?
follow_ups.question_ko: 정부가 이를 더 엄격히 규제해야 할까요?
follow_ups.sample_answer: I think clear standards would help, because voluntary schemes vary so much. Without rules, honest companies can be undercut by those who just make claims.

follow_ups.question: Can you name a company that does this well?
follow_ups.question_ko: 이 부분을 잘하는 회사를 꼽을 수 있나요?
follow_ups.sample_answer: Patagonia is often cited, since it ties its repair and recycling programmes to the core business. It feels authentic rather than decorative.

questions.question: How do you handle it when a project you are leading starts falling behind schedule?
questions.question_ko: 이끌고 있는 프로젝트가 일정에 뒤처지기 시작하면 어떻게 대처하나요?

useful_phrases.text: The first thing I'd do is get a realistic picture of where we stand.
useful_phrases.ko: 가장 먼저 현재 상황을 현실적으로 파악할 거예요.

useful_phrases.text: We may need to re-scope rather than simply work harder.
useful_phrases.ko: 더 열심히 하기보다 범위를 조정해야 할 수도 있어요.

useful_phrases.text: I'd rather flag it early than hide it.

questions.model_answer: The first thing I'd do is get a realistic picture of where we stand, including the root cause of the delay. Is it a resource issue, unclear requirements, or an unexpected technical problem? Then I'd flag it to stakeholders early rather than hide it, because bad news only gets worse with time. Usually we need to re-scope instead of simply working harder, so I'd propose options: cut a feature, extend the deadline, or add resources. I'd recommend one and explain the trade-offs. Afterwards, I'd run a short review to make sure we learn why our original estimate was off.
questions.model_answer_ko: 가장 먼저 지연의 근본 원인을 포함해 현재 상황을 현실적으로 파악할 거예요. 자원 문제인지, 불분명한 요구사항인지, 예상치 못한 기술 문제인지요. 그다음 숨기지 않고 이해관계자에게 일찍 알릴 거예요. 나쁜 소식은 시간이 갈수록 더 나빠지니까요. 보통은 단순히 더 열심히 하는 대신 범위를 조정해야 해서 기능을 줄이거나, 기한을 늘리거나, 인력을 추가하는 선택지를 제안할 거예요. 하나를 추천하며 트레이드오프를 설명하고요. 이후에는 짧은 회고로 처음 추정이 왜 틀렸는지 배우도록 할 거예요.

follow_ups.question: How do you avoid underestimating timelines in the first place?
follow_ups.question_ko: 애초에 일정을 과소평가하지 않으려면 어떻게 하나요?
follow_ups.sample_answer: I add a buffer based on similar past projects and ask the people doing the work for their estimates. Estimates from the top tend to be optimistic.

follow_ups.question: What if the client refuses to move the deadline?
follow_ups.sample_answer: Then we'd negotiate the scope. I'd show what can be delivered by the date and what would follow in a second phase.

follow_ups.question: How do you keep the team motivated during a stressful delay?
follow_ups.question_ko: 스트레스 많은 지연 중에 팀의 동기를 어떻게 유지하나요?
follow_ups.sample_answer: I stay calm, protect them from unnecessary pressure, and celebrate small milestones. Being clear about the plan reduces anxiety a lot.

questions.question: Do you think a university degree is still necessary for a successful career?
questions.question_ko: 성공적인 커리어에 대학 학위가 여전히 필요하다고 생각하세요?

useful_phrases.text: It very much depends on the field.
A degree can open doors, but it doesn't guarantee success.
useful_phrases.ko: 학위가 문을 열어 줄 수는 있지만 성공을 보장하진 않아요.

useful_phrases.text: Employers are increasingly focusing on demonstrable skills.
useful_phrases.ko: 고용주들은 점점 증명 가능한 역량에 초점을 맞춰요.

questions.model_answer: It very much depends on the field. For medicine or engineering, a degree is obviously essential, but in areas like design or software, a strong portfolio can matter more. A degree can open doors, particularly early in a career, but it doesn't guarantee success. Employers are increasingly focusing on demonstrable skills, and online courses and certifications make it easier to acquire them. Still, I'd argue that university offers something that is hard to replace: the chance to build a network and learn how to think critically. So I wouldn't call it unnecessary, but I would say it's no longer the only route.
questions.model_answer_ko: 분야에 따라 크게 달라요. 의학이나 공학에서는 학위가 분명 필수지만, 디자인이나 소프트웨어 같은 분야에서는 탄탄한 포트폴리오가 더 중요할 수 있어요. 학위는 특히 커리어 초기에 문을 열어 줄 수 있지만 성공을 보장하진 않아요. 고용주들은 점점 증명 가능한 역량에 초점을 맞추고, 온라인 강의와 자격증 덕분에 역량을 쌓기도 쉬워졌어요. 그래도 대학은 대체하기 어려운 것, 즉 인맥을 쌓고 비판적으로 사고하는 법을 배울 기회를 준다고 생각해요. 그래서 불필요하다고는 않겠지만 더 이상 유일한 길은 아니라고 말하고 싶어요.

follow_ups.question: Would you advise your own child to go to university?
follow_ups.sample_answer: Probably, but I'd encourage them to think about what they want to gain from it. Going just because everyone else does is a poor reason.

follow_ups.question: Is the cost of higher education justified?
follow_ups.sample_answer: In many countries, the costs have risen faster than the benefits. I think students should weigh the likely return carefully.

follow_ups.question: What skills do universities fail to teach?
follow_ups.sample_answer: Practical ones such as negotiating, managing people, and handling ambiguity. Most of us learn those on the job.

questions.question: How do you build trust quickly with a new team or a new client?
questions.question_ko: 새로운 팀이나 고객과 빠르게 신뢰를 쌓으려면 어떻게 하나요?

useful_phrases.text: I start by listening more than I talk.
Trust is built through small, consistent actions.
I make a point of following through on what I say.

questions.model_answer: I start by listening more than I talk. In the first few weeks, I want to understand people's concerns and what has gone wrong in the past. Trust is built through small, consistent actions, so I make a point of following through on every commitment, even minor ones like sending a promised document on time. I'm also honest about what I don't know, which paradoxically makes people trust me more. With a client, I try to deliver an early, visible win to show we're reliable. Over time, that consistency matters far more than any impressive first meeting.
questions.model_answer_ko: 말하기보다 듣는 것으로 시작해요. 처음 몇 주 동안은 사람들의 우려와 과거에 무엇이 잘못됐는지 이해하고 싶어요. 신뢰는 작고 일관된 행동으로 쌓이니까, 약속한 자료를 제때 보내는 것 같은 사소한 일까지 모든 약속을 지키려고 해요. 모르는 것을 솔직히 인정하는데, 역설적으로 그게 신뢰를 높여 줘요. 고객에게는 우리가 믿을 만하다는 걸 보여 주려고 일찍 눈에 보이는 성과를 내려 해요. 시간이 지나면 인상적인 첫 미팅보다 그 일관성이 훨씬 중요해요.

follow_ups.question: How do you rebuild trust after making a mistake?
follow_ups.sample_answer: I own up to it immediately, explain what I'm doing to fix it, and make sure it doesn't happen again. Excuses make it worse.

follow_ups.question: Is it harder to build trust remotely?
follow_ups.sample_answer: Yes, because you miss the informal signals. I compensate with more frequent, clear communication and the occasional video call.

follow_ups.question: What destroys trust fastest?
follow_ups.sample_answer: Inconsistency between words and actions, I'd say. Being caught in a lie, even a small one, can undo months of effort.

questions.question: What is your opinion on the four-day work week?

useful_phrases.text: The evidence so far seems encouraging.
It wouldn't suit every industry equally.
useful_phrases.ko: 모든 산업에 똑같이 맞지는 않을 거예요.

useful_phrases.text: What matters is output, not hours.

questions.model_answer: The evidence so far seems encouraging, as several pilot programmes have reported stable productivity and higher employee satisfaction. What matters is output, not hours, and many of us spend part of the week in meetings that add little value. A shorter week forces companies to cut that waste. However, it wouldn't suit every industry equally; hospitals or customer support teams would need complicated shift arrangements. I'd also be concerned about people simply cramming five days of work into four and feeling more stressed. So I'd support it, provided it's introduced with realistic workload expectations.
questions.model_answer_ko: 지금까지의 근거는 고무적으로 보여요. 여러 시범 프로그램에서 생산성은 유지되고 직원 만족도는 높아졌다고 보고했거든요. 중요한 건 시간이 아니라 성과이고, 우리 중 많은 사람이 일주일의 일부를 별 가치 없는 회의로 보내요. 단축 근무는 회사가 그런 낭비를 줄이게 만들어요. 다만 모든 산업에 똑같이 맞지는 않아서, 병원이나 고객 지원팀은 복잡한 교대 체계가 필요할 거예요. 5일 치 일을 4일에 욱여넣어 더 스트레스받을까 하는 우려도 있어요. 그래서 현실적인 업무량 기대치를 전제로 도입한다면 찬성해요.

follow_ups.question: Would you accept a pay cut for a shorter week?
follow_ups.sample_answer: Probably a small one, if the extra day really improved my quality of life. But a large cut would be hard to justify.

follow_ups.question: How might it affect career progression?
follow_ups.sample_answer: If everyone adopts it, there's no penalty. In a mixed environment, though, people working longer hours might be seen as more committed, which is unfair.

follow_ups.question: What would you do with an extra day off?
follow_ups.sample_answer: I'd spend part of it on exercise and learning, and part on family. It would make me more focused in the other four days.

questions.question: How do you handle criticism of your work from a senior person?
questions.question_ko: 고위 인사에게 업무에 대한 비판을 받으면 어떻게 대처하나요?

useful_phrases.text: I try not to take it personally.
I ask clarifying questions to understand the root of the concern.
useful_phrases.ko: 우려의 핵심을 이해하려고 확인 질문을 해요.

useful_phrases.text: I see it as an opportunity to improve.

questions.model_answer: I try not to take it personally, although that's easier said than done. My first reaction is usually to listen without interrupting, and then I ask clarifying questions to understand the root of the concern. Sometimes criticism is really about a misunderstanding of the goal rather than the quality of the work. If the feedback is valid, I thank them and propose how I'll fix it, which shows I'm taking it seriously. If I disagree, I wait until I've calmed down and present my reasoning with evidence. Overall, I see criticism as an opportunity to improve, and senior people tend to notice who responds well.
questions.model_answer_ko: 개인적으로 받아들이지 않으려 하지만 말처럼 쉽지는 않아요. 처음에는 보통 끊지 않고 들은 다음, 우려의 핵심을 이해하려고 확인 질문을 해요. 비판이 작업의 질보다 목표에 대한 오해에서 나오는 경우도 있거든요. 타당한 피드백이면 감사 인사를 하고 어떻게 고칠지 제안하는데, 그러면 진지하게 받아들인다는 게 전해져요. 동의하지 않으면 마음을 가라앉힌 뒤 근거를 들어 제 논리를 설명해요. 전반적으로 비판은 개선의 기회라고 보고, 고위 인사들은 누가 잘 받아들이는지 알아채는 편이에요.

follow_ups.question: Have you ever received feedback that changed your career?
follow_ups.question_ko: 커리어를 바꾼 피드백을 받은 적이 있나요?
follow_ups.sample_answer: Yes, a director once told me my presentations were too detailed for executives. Simplifying them completely changed how I was perceived.

follow_ups.question: How do you tell when criticism is unfair?
follow_ups.sample_answer: I look for specifics. Vague or emotional comments tell me more about their mood, whereas concrete examples are usually worth a second look.

follow_ups.question: Should junior staff challenge their superiors more?
follow_ups.question_ko: 주니어 직원이 상급자에게 더 이의를 제기해야 할까요?
follow_ups.sample_answer: Respectfully, yes. Most leaders would rather hear a concern early than discover a problem later.

questions.question: What role should ethics play in business decisions when profit is at stake?
questions.question_ko: 이익이 걸려 있을 때 비즈니스 의사결정에서 윤리는 어떤 역할을 해야 할까요?

useful_phrases.text: Ethics shouldn't be treated as an afterthought.
In the long run, cutting corners tends to backfire.
useful_phrases.ko: 장기적으로 편법은 역효과를 내는 경향이 있어요.

useful_phrases.text: There are times when we have to accept a lower margin.
useful_phrases.ko: 더 낮은 마진을 받아들여야 할 때도 있어요.

questions.model_answer: Ethics shouldn't be treated as an afterthought, because decisions made purely on profit often create hidden risks. In the long run, cutting corners tends to backfire, whether through legal penalties, a damaged reputation, or losing talented employees who don't want to be associated with it. There are times when we have to accept a lower margin in order to do the right thing, and I think leaders need the courage to say so. A practical safeguard is to ask, 'Would we be comfortable if this decision appeared on the front page?' It's not a perfect test, but it catches many problems early.
questions.model_answer_ko: 윤리는 뒷전으로 취급되어선 안 돼요. 이익만으로 내린 결정은 숨은 위험을 만드는 경우가 많거든요. 장기적으로 편법은 법적 제재든 평판 훼손이든, 그런 일과 엮이기 싫어하는 유능한 직원을 잃는 것이든 역효과를 내는 경향이 있어요. 옳은 일을 하려면 더 낮은 마진을 받아들여야 할 때도 있고, 리더에게는 그렇게 말할 용기가 필요하다고 생각해요. 실용적인 안전장치는 '이 결정이 신문 1면에 나가도 떳떳할까?'라고 묻는 거예요. 완벽한 시험은 아니지만 많은 문제를 일찍 잡아내요.

follow_ups.question: Have you ever faced an ethical dilemma at work?
follow_ups.question_ko: 직장에서 윤리적 딜레마를 겪은 적이 있나요?
follow_ups.sample_answer: Once, I was asked to present figures in an overly optimistic way. I raised it with my manager, and we agreed to include the caveats.

follow_ups.question: Should employees report wrongdoing even if it risks their job?
